issues.description: Entire compiled script is now sent over RPC on every compile, inflating payload for large pipelines
issues.detail: compile_notebook now reads the full script_content and returns it inline in every response. For large notebooks/pipelines this can be many MB shipped on every compile, regardless of whether the user downloads. Consider returning content only on a separate download request, or streaming via a dedicated endpoint.

issues.description: open() lacks explicit encoding and error handling for missing script
issues.detail: The new `open(script_path) as f` relies on the platform default encoding and will raise IOError if the file was not written. Use `open(script_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8')` and handle FileNotFoundError so a partial compile failure does not turn into an unrelated 500.

issues.description: Download icon is not a real button and lacks keyboard accessibility
issues.detail: GetAppIcon is rendered as an SVG with onClick but no role, tabIndex, or keyboard handler. Screen readers and keyboard users cannot trigger it, and titleAccess on an SVG is not equivalent to a button label. Wrap in an IconButton or add role="button", tabIndex=0, and onKeyDown.

issues.description: Download button always renders even when compiledContent is missing
issues.detail: The icon is unconditionally rendered in the success branch, but handleDownloadClick silently no-ops if compiledContent is undefined (e.g., older backend, cached state). Either hide the icon when !props.compiledContent or surface an error toast, so users do not click and get nothing.

issues.description: Filename fallback 'pipeline.kale.py' may not match server-side naming convention
issues.detail: When compiledPath has no '/', the code falls back to 'pipeline.kale.py'. The pipeline name is known elsewhere; using a generic fallback may confuse users who download multiple pipelines. Consider deriving from pipeline.config.pipeline_name or omitting the button when path is unavailable.

issues.description: Blob MIME type 'text/plain' for .py file is fine but inconsistent with usual download patterns
issues.detail: Using 'text/plain' works but 'application/octet-stream' or 'text/x-python' is more conventional for forcing a download of a source file and prevents some browsers from attempting to render. Minor; functionally OK.

review.summary: The PR cleanly adds a download button by piping compiled script content from the backend RPC through to a new click handler. Main concerns: the backend now ships the full script body in every compile response regardless of whether the user downloads, the open() call lacks explicit encoding and error handling, and the download control is an SVG with onClick that is not keyboard-accessible and renders even when compiledContent is unavailable. Minor nits on the fallback filename and MIME type. No P0 blockers, but the payload-size and a11y issues should be addressed before merge.
